title: The Apes were ready, but the path was closed
era: 1995 Type I control using current combat rules
matchup: The Deck against red-green creature aggression
story: My Moat had survived a full turn, and the three Kird Ape s opposite me still waited beside their Taiga . During my opponent's main phase, they cast Disenchant to clear the way. I tapped two Island s for Counterspell and watched Disenchant go to the graveyard. When combat began, the Apes could not be declared as attackers; they lacked flying. My Serra Angel was ready to attack on the following turn. The creature line across the table was still alive, but I was no longer counting its power as damage this combat.
review: Documentary reference deck contains Moat, Serra Angel, Counterspell and Disenchant; opposing Kird Apes/Taiga are hypothetical. Counterspell uses two Islands for UU. Moat restricts attack declarations of nonfliers; it does not destroy or prevent combat damage.
claim: representative reconstruction; not a historical match or quotation
candidateStatus: not accepted; pending ten-article checkpoint and deeper deck research
